newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks watchdog to boost surveillance.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks watchdog to boost surveillance.

text.p: The Jakarta capital markets supervisory agency (Bapepam) signed a memorandum of understanding with the Attorney General's office on Tuesday to cooperate in creating guidelines to deal with criminal acts taking place on the bourse.

"In general, this memorandum is aimed at boosting cooperation between the two institutions in creating guidelines to make a simpler, faster and cheaper investigation as well as prosecution procedures in (matters relating to) the bourse," Attorney General Singgih said in a speech.

Bapepam chairman I Putu Gede Ary Suta said both institutions had agreed to provide courses and training for their employees about criminal prosecution and related laws as well as knowledge of procedures in the stock market.

"In order to improve our surveillance tasks, Bapepam will soon change the organisation structure. We will soon include an investigation bureau and an accounting standard bureau," Ary Suta told journalists.
He said the stock exchange was awaiting approval from President Suharto for the new structure.
Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad said the memorandum was a an important step toward guaranteeing that Indonesia's stock exchange was running well and was well-protected by law.
